about.title: About — Tim Chen
about.description: Tim Chen is a C#/.NET backend engineer. This page covers his experience, language study in Tokyo and JLPT N1, and an engineering reading group.
about.heading: About
about.lead: Yu-Ting Chen. I work on C# and .NET backends, mostly the performance and reliability of existing systems.
about.engineering: Since March 2026 I have been a .NET backend engineer at Gogoro. From August 2020 to April 2023 I was a Product Developer at Titansoft, on REST and gRPC microservices, including an internship there in 2020.
about.projects: Public code includes Discipline App, TimeMiner, Level, and TwStock, a service for Taiwan stock data.
about.japan: From April 2024 to October 2025 I studied at Eastwest Japanese Language School in Tokyo. JLPT N1.
about.sharing: At Titansoft I ran an engineering reading group where we looked at problems from the work.
about.life: Outside work I ride and hike.

tools.title: Developer tools
tools.lead: Timestamp, JSON, YAML, MD5, encoding, JWT, URL, UUID, regex, base conversion, text diff, letter case, and identifier case. After the page loads, the calculations run in this browser.

timestamp.pasteHint: Paste a number to convert. Up to 10 digits is seconds; around 13 digits is milliseconds.
timestamp.dateHint: Without a timezone, this is your computer's local time.
timestamp.offsetHint: Anchored to now. Choose an amount and a unit, and the date and timestamp appear below.

json.shortcut: Any change on the left is formatted on the right. The original text stays as you typed it.

yaml.placeholder: Paste YAML. You can also paste JSON and convert it

md5.drop: Drop a file here, or click to choose
md5.dropHint: Hashed in this browser. Nothing is uploaded

jwt.placeholder: Paste a JWT. A leading Bearer prefix is removed
jwt.secretPlaceholder: Only needed to verify HS256 / HS384 / HS512
jwt.sampleHint: Both samples use the secret: secret
jwt.algNote: Decoding needs no secret, and the token stays on this device. Verification supports HMAC only.

errors.invalid-number: That is not a timestamp. Put dates in the field on the right.
errors.invalid-date: Could not read that date. Try 2024-01-02 15:04:05
errors.invalid-relative: Enter a whole number from 0 up, and choose a unit.
errors.invalid-utf8: Those bytes are not valid UTF-8 text
errors.invalid-jwt: That does not look like a JWT. It needs header.payload.signature
errors.out-of-range: That time is outside the supported range
errors.unsupported-alg: Only HS256, HS384, and HS512 can be verified
errors.yaml-missing: The YAML parser did not load
errors.too-large: More than 400 lines. Shorten the text before comparing.

url.placeholder: Paste text, a URL, or a=1&b=2

uuid.hint: Uses this browser’s random numbers. Nothing is sent away.

radix.placeholder: Paste a number, such as 255 or 0xff

tools.pageDescription: Timestamp, JSON, YAML, hashes, encoding, JWT, URL, UUID, regex, base conversion, text diff, letter case, and identifier case in the browser.

diff.hint: Compared line by line. Newlines are normalized first, and a final newline does not count as a difference.

letters.placeholder: Paste English, for example the quick brown fox
letters.hint: Upper and lower case keep the original punctuation. Title case capitalizes each word. Sentence case capitalizes the start of each sentence.
letters.title: Title Case

case.hint: A run of capitals stays one word, so HTTPResponse splits into http and response.

work.description: Tim Chen's work cases and public code.
work.title: Work
work.lead: Work cases are above. Public code is below.
work.case1Title: A checksum mismatch caused extra fallback calls
work.case1Problem: When the checksum did not match, the system called a fallback API again. Those calls were about 75,000 a day, and most of them were unnecessary.
work.case1Action: I found and fixed the checksum mismatch so those fallback calls were no longer sent.
work.case1Result: Daily calls to that fallback API fell from about 75,000 to under 50.
work.case2Problem: Some APIs took more than 2 seconds to respond.
work.case2Action: I changed the APIs that were actually slow.
work.case2Result: Those APIs now respond in about 200 milliseconds.
work.case3Title: Maintenance-notice calculation was hard to test alone
work.case3Problem: Calculation and the service were written together, and the clock was hard to replace, so station data, merged time ranges, and the cache were hard to test on their own.
work.case3Action: I split calculation from the service, injected the clock, and added tests for aggregation, range merging, and caching.
work.case3Result: Range merging and the cache can be tested on their own. Over the same period, the existing unit tests grew from 41 to 240, and the ones that had been failing were fixed.
